22-2.inPlainWords: A shop, restaurant or entertainment venue must display its price list before you order. Charging more than the displayed price, or adding an undisclosed service charge, is an unfair trade practice under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019. Ask for the menu or the rate card, keep the bill, and complain to the consumer commission or the National Consumer Helpline on 1915.
22-2.benefit: The Legal Metrology (Packaged Commodities) Rules, 2011 and the state shops rules require a displayed price. The Consumer Protection Act, 2019 prohibits an unfair trade practice and a misleading price. A restaurant may add a service charge only if it is disclosed; you can ask for it to be removed. The bill must show the tax and the total. A complaint can lead to a refund and compensation.
22-2.cost: No cost. Ask for the price list before you order and keep the bill.
22-2.caveats: A 'market price' item should be quoted before cooking. A service charge is not a tip. A venue's 'minimum charge' should be displayed.
22-2.sources: Consumer Protection Act, 2019. <https://consumeraffairs.nic.in/>; Department of Consumer Affairs, Legal Metrology. <https://consumeraffairs.nic.in/>; National Consumer Helpline. <https://consumerhelpline.gov.in/>
